title: Uterotonics and other obstetric medicines
blurb: Use oxytocin, ergometrine, carboprost, misoprostol, tranexamic acid and magnesium sulfate safely: doses, contraindications, sequence and monitoring.
question: Sofia has severe pre-eclampsia and has been on magnesium sulfate for 6 hours. She is drowsy, her respiratory rate is 9 per minute and her patellar reflexes are absent. What should the midwife do?

teach.h: Uterotonics: drugs that make the uterus contract
teach.body: Formally, uterotonics are medicines that stimulate contraction of the uterine muscle. In plain English: they squeeze the uterus so that the blood vessels at the placental site are clamped shut. Midwives use them to prevent postpartum haemorrhage (active third stage), to treat bleeding from a poorly contracted uterus (atony), and oxytocin is also used to strengthen contractions in labour. Two other obstetric medicines sit alongside: tranexamic acid for bleeding and magnesium sulfate for eclampsia.

teach.h: Oxytocin or ergometrine: speed and staying power
teach.caption: Timings from the note to NG235 table 12. If other drugs are unavailable, for example at a home birth, a repeat dose of ergometrine or oxytocin plus ergometrine may be given.

teach.body: When oxytocin is used to augment labour: offer an epidural before starting; increase the dose no more often than every 30 minutes; aim for 3 to 4 contractions in 10 minutes; reduce or stop it if there are more than 4 in 10; and stop it immediately if the CTG is pathological. A vaginal examination is offered 4 hours after regular contractions begin on oxytocin.

steps.sub: ergometrine IM (carboprost if contraindicated) or oxytocin infusion

steps.sub: second line carboprost IM; further: carboprost repeated (15 min+, max 8) or misoprostol 800 micrograms

teach.h: Worked scenario: Sofia on magnesium sulfate
teach.body: Absent patellar reflexes, a respiratory rate of 9 and drowsiness are signs of magnesium toxicity. The midwife stops the infusion, calls for urgent help (obstetrician and anaesthetist), supports her airway and breathing with oxygen, and prepares calcium gluconate, the antidote, for the doctor to prescribe. When Sofia gives birth, ergometrine-containing uterotonics are contraindicated because of her pre-eclampsia, so oxytocin alone is used for the third stage.
teach.cite: BNF magnesium sulfate; emc SPC 13169; NICE NG235 1.10.9

teach.text: Classic trap: reaching for ergometrine (or Syntometrine) in a woman with severe hypertension or pre-eclampsia. It raises blood pressure and is contraindicated: use oxytocin, then carboprost or an oxytocin infusion for atony. Second trap: with magnesium sulfate, loss of the patellar reflex comes before respiratory depression, so check reflexes, not just the drip rate.

items: Third stage: oxytocin 10 units IM; oxytocin + ergometrine if no contraindication.
Ergometrine: not in pre-eclampsia, eclampsia, severe hypertension or severe cardiac, hepatic, renal disease.
Carboprost IM, repeat at 15 minutes or more up to 8 doses; misoprostol 800 micrograms SL or PR.
Tranexamic acid 1 g IV over 10 minutes, repeat after 30 minutes or more if still bleeding.
Magnesium sulfate 4 g IV then 1 g/hour for 24 h; watch reflexes and breathing; antidote calcium gluconate.

summary: You can now choose and give uterotonics in the right order for the woman in front of you, avoiding ergometrine where it is contraindicated. You can also give tranexamic acid correctly and monitor magnesium sulfate, recognising and acting on toxicity.

A.q: Amina has pre-eclampsia and received oxytocin 10 units IM for the third stage. She now has a PPH with a soft, boggy uterus. Which uterotonic is the most appropriate next drug?
A.why: NG235 table 12: after oxytocin alone, give ergometrine IM or, if contraindicated, carboprost (or an oxytocin infusion). Pre-eclampsia contraindicates ergometrine, so carboprost is appropriate.

whyNot.0: Ergometrine is contraindicated in pre-eclampsia (NG235 1.10.9; BNF).
whyNot.2: The combination contains ergometrine, which is contraindicated in pre-eclampsia.
whyNot.3: Table 12 lists misoprostol among the further treatments after first-line drugs, not before them.

A.q: A woman is bleeding after birth despite uterotonics. The obstetrician prescribes tranexamic acid. How is it given?
options: 2 g IV as a rapid bolus
500 mg by mouth three times a day
A.why: NG235 1.10.35: tranexamic acid 1 g by intravenous injection over 10 minutes, repeated after at least 30 minutes if bleeding continues.

whyNot.0: The PPH dose is 1 g, given over 10 minutes, not a rapid 2 g bolus.
whyNot.1: Oral tranexamic acid is not the treatment for acute PPH.
whyNot.3: Tranexamic acid for PPH is given intravenously.

A.q: Carboprost has been given for uterine atony and bleeding continues. What does NICE say about repeating it?
options: Intervals of 15 minutes or more, max 8 doses
Intervals of 5 minutes or more, max 3 doses
Intervals of 30 minutes or more, max 4 doses
Intervals of 1 hour or more, max 6 doses
A.why: NG235 table 12: carboprost can be repeated at intervals of not less than 15 minutes, up to a maximum of 8 doses.

whyNot.1: 5-minute intervals are too short, and the maximum is 8 doses.
whyNot.2: 30 minutes is longer than needed, and the maximum is 8 doses.
whyNot.3: Hourly repeats would delay treatment; the interval is 15 minutes or more.

B.q: Leah is on an oxytocin infusion for delay in the first stage. The midwife counts 5 contractions in 10 minutes and the CTG is normal. What should she do?
options: Continue at this rate and review in 30 minutes
Increase the rate to settle the pattern
Give ergometrine IM to regulate the uterus
Reduce or stop the oxytocin infusion
B.why: NG235 1.8.55: if there are more than 4 contractions in 10 minutes, reduce or stop the oxytocin.

whyNot.0: More than 4 in 10 needs action now, not continued infusion.
whyNot.1: Increasing the rate would make overstimulation worse.
whyNot.2: Ergometrine causes sustained contraction and has no role in labour.

B.q: Which observation is used to detect magnesium sulfate toxicity early?
B.why: BNF and the SPC: loss of patellar reflexes is a sign of overdose; NICE NG25 asks for patellar reflexes with pulse, BP and respiratory rate at least every 4 hours.

whyNot.0: Glucose is not a marker of magnesium toxicity.
whyNot.2: Temperature does not detect magnesium toxicity.
whyNot.3: Pupil checks are not the recommended toxicity monitoring.

B.q: Kemi has an eclamptic seizure. Which magnesium sulfate regimen does NICE NG133 recommend?
options: 2 g IV over 1 hour, then 2 g/hour for the next 12 hours
4 g IM, then 1 g IM every 4 hours
4 g IV over 5–15 minutes, then 1 g/hour for 24 hours
B.why: NG133 1.8.4: loading dose 4 g IV over 5-15 minutes, then 1 g/hour for 24 hours (continued for 24 hours after the last fit).

whyNot.0: This is not the Collaborative Eclampsia Trial regimen used by NICE.
whyNot.3: Diazepam and phenytoin are not to be used as alternatives (NG133 1.8.5).

C.q: Sofia has severe pre-eclampsia and has been on magnesium sulfate for 6 hours. She is drowsy, her respiratory rate is 9 per minute and her patellar reflexes are absent. What should the midwife do first?
options: Stop the infusion and call for urgent help
Continue and recheck reflexes in 4 hours
Increase the rate as she may be about to fit
Give IV diazepam to prevent a seizure
C.why: Absent reflexes and respiratory depression are signs of magnesium toxicity: stop the infusion, call for urgent help, support breathing and prepare calcium gluconate, the antidote (BNF; SPC).

whyNot.1: These are toxicity signs; waiting 4 hours could lead to respiratory arrest.
whyNot.2: Increasing the rate would worsen toxicity.
whyNot.3: Diazepam is not an alternative to magnesium sulfate in eclampsia (NG133 1.8.5) and would further depress breathing.

C.q: At a home birth, Jess has a PPH after oxytocin plus ergometrine IM. The midwife has called 999, is massaging the uterus and has emptied the bladder. Her kit holds oxytocin and oxytocin plus ergometrine. What should she give?
options: Repeat the oxytocin plus ergometrine dose
No further drug until the paramedics arrive
A second dose of oxytocin 2 units IV
C.why: NG235 table 12 note: a repeat dose of ergometrine or oxytocin plus ergometrine may be given if other medicines are not available, for example in a home birth setting.

whyNot.1: Waiting delays treatment of an ongoing haemorrhage.
whyNot.2: Tranexamic acid for PPH is given IV and is not a midwives exemption medicine.
whyNot.3: This is not a recognised dose or route for treating PPH.

C.q: Hannah has severe cardiac disease. She received oxytocin 10 units IM for the third stage and is now bleeding from an atonic uterus. Which first-line uterotonic is most appropriate?
options: An oxytocin infusion via IV access
Oxytocin plus ergometrine by IM injection
C.why: After oxytocin alone, NICE offers ergometrine (carboprost if contraindicated) or an oxytocin infusion. Ergometrine is contraindicated in severe cardiac disease and carboprost in cardiac disease (BNF), so the oxytocin infusion is safest.

whyNot.0: Ergometrine is contraindicated in severe cardiac disease (BNF; NG235 1.10.9).
whyNot.1: Carboprost is contraindicated in cardiac disease (BNF).
whyNot.3: The combination contains ergometrine, which is contraindicated here.

reteach.title: Match the drug to the woman
reteach.question: Before reaching for a uterotonic, what two things about the woman must you know?

blocks.h: What has she had, and what can she not have?
blocks.body: First: what did she receive in the third stage? That decides the next drug in NICE table 12. Second: what are her contraindications? Severe hypertension, pre-eclampsia, eclampsia and severe cardiac, liver or kidney disease rule out ergometrine; cardiac or lung disease rules out carboprost. An oxytocin infusion is usually an option for everyone. Tranexamic acid is added to uterotonics, not used instead.

blocks.text: Magnesium toxicity sequence to remember: reflexes go first, then breathing slows. Stop the infusion, call for help, calcium gluconate is the antidote.

explain.body: Oxytocin 10 units IM is the standard third-stage drug. After IM injection it acts in about 2.5 minutes and lasts about 30 minutes to 1 hour (NG235 table 12 note). In labour, titrate it to 3-4 contractions in 10 minutes.

test.q: After an IM injection, about how quickly does oxytocin begin to act?
test.why: NG235 table 12 note: after IM administration oxytocin acts in about 2.5 minutes.

whyNot.0: About 7 minutes is the onset of ergometrine.
whyNot.2: 15-20 minutes is far slower than oxytocin's onset.
whyNot.3: 30 minutes to 1 hour is how long oxytocin's effect lasts, not its onset.

explain.body: Ergometrine causes a sustained contraction lasting about 3 hours but raises blood pressure. It is contraindicated in severe hypertension, pre-eclampsia, eclampsia and severe cardiac, hepatic or renal disease (NG235 1.10.9).

test.q: Which condition is a contraindication to ergometrine?
test.why: NG235 1.10.9: oxytocin plus ergometrine is contraindicated in severe hypertension, pre-eclampsia, eclampsia and severe cardiac, hepatic or renal disease.

whyNot.0: A previous PPH is a risk factor, not a contraindication.
whyNot.1: Twins raise PPH risk; they do not contraindicate ergometrine.
whyNot.2: Prolonged labour is a PPH risk factor, not a contraindication.

explain.body: Carboprost IM can be repeated at intervals of 15 minutes or more, up to 8 doses; avoid it in cardiac or pulmonary disease. Misoprostol 800 micrograms sublingually or rectally is an option, and may be used earlier if there is no IV access (NG235 table 12).

test.q: What dose and route of misoprostol does NICE list for treating PPH?
options: 8 mg sublingually as a single dose
test.why: NG235 table 12: misoprostol 800 micrograms sublingually or rectally (an off-label use).

whyNot.2: Misoprostol is not given intramuscularly, and 200 micrograms is not the PPH dose.
whyNot.3: 8 mg is a thousand-fold error: the dose is in micrograms.

explain.body: Monitor BP, respiratory rate, urine output and patellar reflexes. Loss of patellar reflexes and respiratory depression mean toxicity. Calcium gluconate is the antidote (BNF; SPC).

test.q: What is the antidote for magnesium sulfate toxicity?
test.why: The magnesium sulfate SPC names calcium gluconate as the antidote for toxicity.

whyNot.1: Sodium bicarbonate does not reverse magnesium toxicity.
whyNot.3: Potassium chloride is not an antidote and strong potassium is a known Never Event risk.
